key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation plus ANN surrogate can accurately predict and optimize friction stir welding quality in HDPE, especially when bottom preheating stabilizes heat flow and axial force.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical process-map for selecting spindle speed, traverse speed, and preheat settings to reduce defects and improve joint consistency in thermoplastic welding.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model for thermal-mechanical FSW behavior
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temporal temperature and force data
Process-window mapping across rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong predictive performance with R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, while CEL results matched experiments for void formation, temperature, and force trends.
watch_item: The workflow is validated on a limited HDPE parameter space, so performance may drop when transferred to other polymers, tool geometries, or broader operating ranges.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
